editorial.headline: Root Vegetable Farming, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated farming of tuber and allium vegetables, from land preparation through post-harvest work, with full foreign ownership available nationally.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01134 is the farming code for root and bulb vegetables when the agricultural work is carried as one connected activity.** In practical terms, it covers crops such as potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots, Chinese radish, bamboo shoots, garlic, onions, shallots, leeks, and other alliaceous vegetables. The scope is not limited to the moment of planting. It also includes land preparation, nursery and seed activities for these horticultural vegetables, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling when those steps form a single operating chain.

That integrated-chain point matters. A founder using this code is describing a farming activity, not merely trading vegetables after someone else has grown them. The record points to the productive cycle: preparing the land, sowing or seeding, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the post-harvest stage as part of the same horticultural operation. For a business plan, the centre of gravity is therefore cultivation of tuber and bulb vegetables, with the supporting nursery, seed, and post-harvest work attached to that farming activity rather than presented as a separate line of business.

The code is available across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national investment list does not cap foreign ownership below full ownership for this activity. That does not, by itself, make every location and operating scale frictionless; it simply defines the national foreign-investment position contained in the record.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is not a hidden block. The provincial moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This record, however, marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is that this farming activity is nationally foreign-open and, on the record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by that moratorium. The caution is narrower: Bali’s status here comes from the risk position at Besar scale, so the registration analysis should stay anchored to the exact scale and activity chain being filed, not to a generic idea of agriculture.
